items.title: Peel Region's South Asian Film Festival Marks 15 Years With a Shift Toward Local Talent
items.summary: According to CBC, the International Film Festival of South Asia is celebrating its 15th year as a Peel Region cultural institution. The outlet reports the anniversary marks a turning point for the festival, which started out curating films from around the world and is now building an ecosystem meant to help local South Asian filmmakers get their work made and seen. CBC Peel's Nav Nanwa hosted this year's gala on Friday in Brampton, a city that sits alongside Mississauga in the heart of the GTA's South Asian community. Nanwa spoke with organizers and attendees before taking the stage, gathering their reflections on how far the festival has come. CBC says the milestone event highlights the growing presence of homegrown South Asian filmmaking talent across the region.

items.title: Mississauga Mayoral Candidate Channels Bollywood to Promise No Property Tax Hike
items.summary: According to the Deccan Chronicle, Mississauga mayoral candidate Dipika Damerla is drawing attention in Ontario's municipal election with a campaign video built around a reworked Bollywood song. The outlet reports Damerla, born in Secunderabad, completed her MBA in Toronto before winning election to Mississauga city council in 2018. She went on to serve seven years as the Ontario Liberal MPP for Mississauga East-Cooksville, including time as associate minister for long-term care and later as minister responsible for seniors affairs. The Deccan Chronicle says Damerla worked in corporate banking and ran her own business in Mississauga before entering politics. In the video shared on X, she sings a modified version of the Bollywood song 'Kya Hua Tera Wada' and pledges that property taxes will not rise if she becomes mayor. The outlet reports the video closes with her campaign slogan, 'A city that works,' alongside an appeal for voter support. The City of Mississauga's own website confirms Damerla served as the Ward 7 councillor beginning in 2018.

items.title: Here's What ID Voters Need to Bring to Advance Polls in Ontario's Municipal Election
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, advance polls have opened in parts of Ontario ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election, and voters need to bring proper identification to cast a ballot. The outlet reports a Canadian passport does not count as valid ID for voting purposes, since voters write their own address inside it rather than having it printed by the issuing authority. Mississauga.com says residents who are currently unhoused, or whose identification has been lost or stolen, still have options available to them to vote without standard ID. The outlet is encouraging voters to confirm exactly when and where advance polls are open in their own community ahead of election day. Mississauga.com reports the identification rules apply across the province as municipalities prepare for the Oct. 26 vote.

items.title: Mississauga Council Creates Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force to Guide Future Planning Rules
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city council unanimously approved a motion from Coun. Sue McFadden on Sept. 29 to create a temporary task force focused on shaping planning rules around large-scale data centres. The outlet reports the task force will include council members, municipal planning staff, industry representatives and local residents, and is meant to operate on a short-term basis. McFadden told council it was important to bring in residents from wards 9 and 10, where applications for hyperscale data centres have been most active. Mississauga.com says the task force decision comes two weeks after council approved a temporary two-year freeze, through an interim control bylaw passed Sept. 16, on new and existing data centre applications across the city. The outlet reports the task force is meant to help guide the city's broader planning review while that freeze stays in effect.

items.title: Discount Retailer Returns to Oakville With 30,000 Square Feet of Liquidation Deals Near Mississauga Border
items.summary: According to Insauga, Clearance Warehouse plans to open a new 30,000-square-foot location in Oakville next month, near the Mississauga border, offering discounts of up to 80 per cent off retail prices on household goods, personal care products and kitchen appliances. The outlet reports the store will open at the corner of Ford Drive and Royal Windsor Drive, in the former RONA building, putting it within easy reach of bargain hunters in neighbouring Mississauga. Unlike a traditional retail store, Insauga says Clearance Warehouse operates through limited-time sales built around liquidation, overstock and closeout merchandise, so its inventory and deals change from sale to sale. Typical stock includes kitchenware, small appliances, bedding, household cleaning supplies, health and beauty products, clothing, tools and seasonal items. The company does not sell online, meaning shoppers have to visit in person to browse and buy. Insauga notes Clearance Warehouse already runs locations in Brampton and Etobicoke, making the new Oakville store its latest expansion into the western GTA.

items.title: 25th Annual Haunted Mississauga Tour Revives an 1836 Election Gone Violent
items.summary: According to Insauga, Heritage Mississauga's 25th annual Haunted Mississauga Heritage Tour returns this Halloween season with a nighttime walk through Streetsville Memorial Cemetery on Friday, Oct. 23, transporting visitors back to a turbulent 1836 election in Upper Canada. The outlet reports volunteer performers stage live, unscripted theatrical scenes depicting historical characters and events as the group makes its way through the cemetery grounds after dark. This year's theme, called Axe Handles and Whiskey, explores a period when political loyalties ran deep enough that election disputes could turn physically dangerous. Insauga says the roughly 45-minute tour favours storytelling and local history over a traditional haunted house format, blending Halloween atmosphere with real events from the city's past. The tradition traces back to 2002, when an event featuring the late author Terry Boyle, who wrote Haunted Ontario, proved popular enough to spark the annual series. Admission is listed at $5 for adults, with limited spots available at the cemetery, located at 299 Queen St. S.

items.title: Mississauga YouTuber Who Built His Own Police-Tracking Camera Gets a Visit From Police
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga resident and YouTuber Anthony Sistilli received a visit from police after he built his own version of a Flock Safety camera and posted video of himself testing it near Shopper's World in Brampton. Insauga reports Flock is a U.S. manufacturer and operator of surveillance hardware, including networks of automated licence plate readers that can reconstruct where people have travelled and when. The outlet points to a Washington Post investigation that found some police departments used Flock cameras to track down ex-partners, raising concerns about unauthorized access to the surveillance data. Brampton announced a $4-million program for 50 of the cameras in March 2025, and by May the city said the devices, equipped with 360-degree imaging and licence plate recognition, were already providing police with evidence in cases ranging from auto theft to violent crime. Sistilli told Insauga that American jurisdictions have portals letting the public see logs of what officers search for in the system, but Canadians have no comparable way to access those records. Insauga reports Sistilli used his demonstration to criticize what he sees as a lack of transparency around how the cameras are used in Canada.
